snippet.title: Giuseppe Morabito "U Tiradrittu" - Chef der ’Ndrangheta - Doku
snippet.description:
Giuseppe Morabito steht für eine Form von Macht, die im Verborgenen gewachsen ist. Aufgewachsen im abgelegenen Africo im Aspromonte, erlebte er den Wandel der ’Ndrangheta von einer regional verankerten Struktur hin zu einem international vernetzten kriminellen System.

Dieses Video beleuchtet die sozialen und historischen Hintergründe Kalabriens, die internen Konflikte der Organisation sowie Morabitos Rolle als strategischer Akteur, der Konflikte ausglich, Allianzen formte und Entscheidungen beeinflusste, ohne selbst im Vordergrund zu stehen. Sein Einfluss reichte weit über Kalabrien hinaus und prägte neue Wege der illegalen Wirtschaft in Italien und darüber hinaus.

Ein Schwerpunkt liegt auf seiner jahrelangen Flucht innerhalb Kalabriens, die ohne moderne Kommunikation und fernab öffentlicher Aufmerksamkeit stattfand, sowie auf seiner Festnahme, die von Ermittlern als Wendepunkt im Kampf gegen die ’Ndrangheta bewertet wurde.

Eine dokumentarische Analyse darüber, wie sich organisierte Kriminalität an gesellschaftliche Veränderungen anpasst – und welche Rolle stille Machtfiguren dabei spielen.

snippet.title: Denver-Clan-Star Catherine Oxenberg – und ihr tragisches Schicksa
snippet.description:
Catherine Oxenberg war als „Denver-Clan"-Star und echte Königs-Nachfahrin ein Weltstar – doch das eigentliche Drama ihres Lebens begann erst später.
In dieser Doku erzählen wir die ganze Geschichte von Catherine Oxenberg: geboren in den europäischen Hochadel, als Urenkelin der serbischen Königsfamilie Karađorđević, deren Großvater Prinz Paul von Jugoslawien Thron und Heimat im Exil verlor. In Hollywood spielte sie ausgerechnet Prinzessin Diana und wurde als Amanda Carrington im „Denver-Clan" weltberühmt – gesehen von bis zu 100 Millionen Menschen pro Woche. Doch hinter dem Glanz lagen ein Karriereknick, eine Ehe, die nur neun Tage hielt – und schließlich der Albtraum, der alles überschattete: Ihre Tochter India geriet in die als Selbsthilfe getarnte Sex-Sekte NXIVM, wurde gebrandmarkt, und Catherine kämpfte jahrelang gegen Sektenführer Keith Raniere, um ihr Kind zu retten.
Wenn dir solche wahren Schicksale hinter berühmten Namen gefallen, abonniere den Kanal und lass ein Like da. Schreib uns in die Kommentare: Wusstest du, dass die „Denver-Clan"-Schauspielerin aus einer echten Königsfamilie stammt?

snippet.title: El Z-40: Llora en su celda sin ventanas
snippet.description:
Lo que está pasando con el Zeta 40 dentro de una celda sin ventanas en Warsaw, Virginia, es quizás la historia más escalofriante que ha producido el crimen organizado en los últimos años, no por lo que él hizo, sino por lo que ahora le están haciendo a él. Miguel Ángel Treviño Morales, el hombre que lideró a los Zetas durante su etapa más sangrienta, el capo que ordenó decapitaciones como herramienta de comunicación, que quemó cuerpos vivos y ejecutó personalmente a sus víctimas porque no confiaba en nadie para algo tan importante, lleva más de doscientos setenta y cinco días en confinamiento solitario absoluto en una cárcel regional del condado de Richmond, Virginia.

Sus propios abogados han presentado ante un tribunal federal documentos clínicos que describen estrés extremo, ansiedad severa y depresión profunda. El hombre que paralizaba ciudades enteras en Tamaulipas, Nuevo León y Coahuila con solo mencionar su apodo, está pidiendo compasión a un juez. Le piden que le dejen ver la luz del sol aunque sea una hora al día.

En este documental analizamos en profundidad los documentos judiciales del distrito este de Virginia, las transcripciones de audiencias, las declaraciones de sus abogados y los testimonios de sobrevivientes de sus operaciones. Reconstruimos la historia completa del Zeta Cuarenta: su origen en Nuevo Laredo, su ascenso dentro del Cártel del Golfo y los Zetas, los métodos que lo convirtieron en uno de los capos más temidos y violentos del narcotráfico mexicano, y la operación del sistema federal estadounidense que lo colocó en el lugar más invisible posible para las organizaciones que querrían localizarlo.

La celda mide dos metros con diez de ancho por dos metros con setenta de largo. Sin ventanas. Sin luz natural. Sin contacto con otros presos. Veinticuatro horas continuas de aislamiento total, donde el fluorescente no distingue entre el martes y el domingo, entre las tres de la tarde y las tres de la madrugada. Todo lo que él les hizo a otros, el sistema se lo está haciendo a él. No como coincidencia. Como consecuencia.

snippet.title: JUNIOR ROLDÁN: El Narco que Gobernó desde su CELDA
snippet.description:
Hay nombres que no se pronuncian en voz alta. En Ecuador, uno de esos nombres es Junior Roldán. Un hombre que gobernó prisiones enteras desde su celda, que movió millones en el corazón del crimen organizado ecuatoriano, que sobrevivió atentados, condenas y persecuciones... y que un día simplemente desapareció. La versión oficial dice que murió en Colombia en mayo de 2023. Pero su tumba fue profanada. Su cuerpo fue robado. Nadie del Estado ecuatoriano vio jamás sus restos. Y meses después de su supuesta muerte, empezaron a circular rumores que cruzaban fronteras. ¿Realmente murió Junior Roldán o planeó su propia desaparición para escapar del hombre más peligroso que jamás tuvo enfrente?

En este documental de crimen organizado recorremos la historia completa de Junior Alexander Roldán Paredes, desde sus orígenes en El Triunfo, en la provincia del Guayas, hasta su meteórico ascenso dentro del narcotráfico ecuatoriano. Un joven reservado y ambicioso que encontró en el crimen organizado el único camino visible en un cantón olvidado por el Estado. Un hombre que construyó su poder con violencia, pero también con imagen: el narco que regalaba en su barrio, pagaba fiestas y compraba lealtades antes de imponer el terror.

Conocerás su relación con Los Choneros, la banda criminal más poderosa de Ecuador, y con su líder Rasquiña. Entenderás cómo una amistad forjada entre rejas cambió para siempre el mapa del crimen organizado en el país. Y descubrirás cómo Ecuador, ubicado entre Colombia y Perú, se convirtió en plataforma clave del tráfico internacional de cocaína con conexiones al Cártel de Sinaloa, la mafia albanesa y la Ndrangheta italiana.

Una historia de poder, traición, narcotráfico y una tumba vacía que todavía no tiene respuesta.

snippet.title: John Gotti - Der Letzte Don - Dokumentation
snippet.description:
John Gotti, bekannt als der „Dapper Don“ und später als „Teflon Don“, war einer der berüchtigtsten Mafia-Bosse des 20. Jahrhunderts. Als Anführer der Gambino-Familie verwandelte er die amerikanische Unterwelt in ein Medienspektakel: maßgeschneiderte Anzüge, öffentliche Auftritte, Provokationen gegenüber der Polizei und ein Charisma, das ihm sowohl Bewunderer als auch erbitterte Feinde einbrachte. Hinter der glamourösen Fassade jedoch stand ein Mann, der zahlreiche brutale Entscheidungen traf, interne Machtkämpfe entfesselte und am Ende durch Verrat seines eigenen Unterbosses stürzte. Gottis Aufstieg und Fall zeigen, wie gefährlich der Mix aus Macht, Ego und öffentlicher Aufmerksamkeit für jeden Anführer der organisierten Kriminalität ist.

snippet.title: The Real 'American Me' Was the Most Dangerous Gang Story Ever Filmed
snippet.description:
On March 25, 1992, just 12 days after American Me premiered in theaters, a gunman walked up behind 53-year-old Charles “Charlie Brown” Manriquez in Ramona Gardens and fired 3 shots into his back. 2 months later, 49-year-old grandmother Ana Lizarraga, the film’s most beloved consultant, was ambushed and gunned down outside her home. The movie meant to scare kids away from gang life had become a death warrant.

In this deep-dive documentary, we uncover the real story behind Edward James Olmos’s 1992 cult classic American Me and the four real men who inspired its most iconic characters.

What you will learn:
- The true biography of Rodolfo “Cheyenne” Cadena, the 16-year-old killer from Bakersfield who became the architect of La Eme
- How Joe “Pegleg” Morgan, a Croatian-American bank robber, became the first non-Mexican godfather of the Mexican Mafia
- The legend of Jap Mike Kudo, the Japanese American who shattered every rule of gang membership
- Why former hitman Ramon “Mundo” Mendoza warned Olmos about the contract on his life and was ignored
- The exact scenes in American Me that the Mexican Mafia considered an unforgivable insult to Cadena’s memory

snippet.title: The Real Nucky Johnson: The Crime Boss Atlantic City Forgot
snippet.description:
On January 13th, 1941, Enoch Lewis Johnson, a central figure in Atlantic City's history, faced sentencing for tax evasion, marking a significant moment in prohibition history. 

Forget Steve Buscemi. The real Enoch “Nucky” Johnson stood 6+ inches tall, weighed 250 pounds, drove a powder-blue Rolls-Royce down the Boardwalk in broad daylight, and personally hosted the 1929 Atlantic City Conference that literally invented modern organized crime in America. He never killed a man. He didn’t need to. He owned the cops who carried the guns.

In this 30-minute deep dive, we go past the HBO sanitization and into the real story of the Atlantic County Treasurer who ran a criminal-political empire for 30 years and pocketed an estimated $500,000 a year in 1920s money — roughly $9 million annually in today’s dollars.

What you’ll learn in this documentary:
• How a 25-year-old sheriff became the most powerful political boss in New Jersey
 • The complete inside story of the May 1929 Atlantic City Conference where Capone, Luciano, Lansky, Torrio, and Costello met at the Ritz-Carlton
 • Why Nucky personally walked Al Capone through the Boardwalk after the Breakers Hotel refused him a room
 • How the National Crime Syndicate and the Commission were actually born on the Atlantic City Boardwalk
 • The exact mechanics of Nucky’s graft machine — bootleggers, brothels, speakeasies, and beat cops on the payroll
 • How the IRS finally cracked the case using the same playbook that took down Capone
 • The 1941 federal trial, the 10-year sentence, and Lewisburg inmate number 7525
 • Nucky’s slow, broken death in a Northfield nursing home in 1968 — blind, forgotten, asking for a red carnation

Key figures: 
Enoch “Nucky” Johnson, Al Capone, Charles “Lucky” Luciano, Meyer Lansky, Johnny Torrio, Frank Costello, Franklin D Roosevelt, IRS Agent William E Frank.

Why this story matters today: The arrangement Nucky pioneered between elected office and organized crime didn’t die when he went to prison. It just got better at hiding. Understanding Nucky Johnson is understanding the blueprint every American political-criminal alliance has copied for nearly a century.

Verified sources referenced in this episode:
 • “Boardwalk Empire: The Birth, High Times, and Corruption of Atlantic City” by Nelson Johnson (Plexus Publishing, 2002) — the definitive biography that inspired the HBO series
 • United States v Enoch L Johnson, federal court records, District of New Jersey, 1939-1941
 • FBI files on the Atlantic City Conference of May 1929, declassified historical archives

This history documentary explores the downfall of the powerful Nucky Johnson, whose reign over organized crime in Atlantic City came to an end. 

It's a true crime story that delves into the real events behind the legends.

snippet.title: Helmut Berger: Der schönste Mann der Welt – und sein Ende
snippet.description:
Helmut Berger galt als der schönste Mann der Welt – Weltstar und Geliebter von Luchino Visconti. Am Ende saß er fast ganz allein.

Vom Gastwirtssohn aus Bad Ischl zum gefeierten Star des europäischen Kinos: Helmut Berger lebte ein Leben wie ein Aristokrat. An der Seite von Luchino Visconti wurde er mit "Die Verdammten" und "Ludwig II." zum Weltstar, posierte als schönster Mann der Welt auf dem Cover der Vogue und feierte mit dem internationalen Jet-Set. Es folgten Geld, Alkohol, Skandale – und 2013 der Auftritt im RTL-Dschungelcamp, der für viele zum traurigen Sinnbild seines Absturzes wurde. October 6, 1977. A car bomb in a Lyndhurst, Ohio parking lot ends the life of Danny Greene, the Celtic Club founder who survived 7 professional assassination attempts and humiliated the entire Cleveland Mafia for nearly a decade. What the Hollywood film “Kill the Irishman” couldn’t show you is darker, stranger, and far more documented than the cinematic version.
In this deep dive investigation, we unpack the real story of Danny Greene, the Marine turned longshoreman turned FBI top-echelon informant who built a criminal empire on Cleveland’s east side while simultaneously feeding intelligence to federal agents for 13 years.

What you’ll learn in this episode:
- How an Irish orphan from Collinwood took on an entire La Cosa Nostra family and won
- The exact mechanics of Greene’s “tax” on Cleveland’s bookmakers, generating $8,000 to $15,000 a week
- The full timeline of all 7 failed assassination attempts between 1975 and 1977
- The murder of Shondor Birns and how Greene killed his own mentor

- The chain reaction that produced 22 federal convictions and destroyed the Cleveland crime family permanently
- How underboss Angelo Lonardo’s cooperation helped Rudy Giuliani destroy the Five Families

Danny Greene, James “Jack White” Licavoli, John Nardi, Shondor Birns, Ray Ferritto, Angelo Lonardo, John Scalish

Every modern federal RICO prosecution traces a line back to Cleveland.

Seven days after the heist, the mob came for Stacks.

snippet.title: ¿Qué pasó con los asesinos de Pablo Escobar?
snippet.description:
Durante quince años fueron la sombra armada de Pablo Escobar. Los hombres que ejecutaron cada atentado, cada magnicidio y cada operación que puso de rodillas a toda Colombia. El Pinina, El Chopo, Tyson, El Arete y El Mugre: los pistoleros más letales del Cartel de Medellín y la historia que nadie se ha atrevido a contar completa hasta ahora.

Este vídeo desvela el ascenso, la caída y los finales radicalmente distintos de cada uno de estos sicarios profesionales que construyeron el aparato de terror más eficiente del narcotráfico colombiano. Hombres nacidos en la pobreza extrema de las comunas del nororiente antioqueño que encontraron en la violencia su única escala social posible. Hombres que mataron por encargo durante una década entera y cuyas historias reales superan cualquier ficción que las series televisivas hayan sido capaces de recrear.

Descubrirás quién fue realmente John Jairo Arias Tascón, el Pinina, jefe militar absoluto del Cartel de Medellín y quinta figura en la jerarquía global de toda la estructura criminal. Conocerás su papel directo en el asesinato del ministro Rodrigo Lara Bonilla, en el atentado al edificio del DAS y en la brutal campaña de exterminio sistemático contra la Policía Nacional. Y sobre todo, descubrirás la pregunta que nadie se hace cuando habla del fin del cartel: si el último hombre que quedó de pie junto a Escobar fue realmente su guardaespaldas más leal o si fue precisamente él quien entregó las coordenadas exactas que sellaron el destino del patrón aquella tarde de diciembre de 1993.

Historias del crimen organizado que cambian la lectura completa de la guerra más brutal que Colombia vivió en el siglo veinte. Porque uno murió en un operativo. Otro de cáncer en una cama de hospital. Otro predica los domingos en una iglesia evangélica. Otro pasea por Barcelona con un nombre que no es el suyo. Y el último descansa a pocos metros de la tumba del patrón, con la sospecha eterna encima de su lápida.

snippet.title: The Last Mafia Fixer Who Controlled the Entire US Justice System
snippet.description:
January 1996. The most powerful mobster in American history died peacefully in his Beverly Hills mansion. No bullets. No prison time. Just billions of dollars and absolute silence. Meet Sidney Korshak, the legendary Chicago Outfit lawyer who traded Tommy guns for legal briefs and quietly conquered the United States.

In this deep-dive MAFIA TALKS documentary, we expose the secret life of the Mafia's ultimate fixer. While famous bosses like Al Capone and John Gotti faced prison or assassination, Korshak built an invisible empire, manipulating Hollywood studios, Vegas casinos, and federal judges—all without leaving a single piece of evidence behind.

What You Will Learn:

How the Chicago Outfit transitioned from street violence to corporate extortion.

The exact mechanics of the Hollywood union strike schemes that cost studios millions.

How Jimmy Hoffa and the Teamsters Pension Fund financed the Las Vegas strip.

The legendary phone call that secured Al Pacino's role in The Godfather.

Why the FBI and Justice Department spent decades trying to catch him, but failed.

Key Figures & Timeline:

1930s-1940s: Korshak defends the Chicago Outfit, learning the fatal flaws of violent extortion from the Willie Bioff scandal.

1946: Relocates to Los Angeles, establishing his command center at the Bistro in Beverly Hills.

1950s-1960s: Brokers massive deals between MCA's Lew Wasserman, the Screen Actors Guild, and the Mob's Vegas expansion.

1976: Exposed by Seymour Hersh in a devastating New York Times series, sparking relentless FBI heat.

1996: Dies of natural causes at 88, having never spent a day in jail.

Why This Story Matters Today:
Korshak's blueprint changed the world. He proved that organized crime doesn't need street corners when it can control boardrooms. His legacy forced law enforcement to adapt, leading to the financial tracking methods and RICO laws used to fight modern corruption today.

snippet.title: She Knew About the Colombo's Secrets — Greg Scarpa Cut Her Into Pieces
snippet.description:
She was not a boss. She was not a soldier. She was not trying to take over the Colombo family. But Mary Bari knew the wrong people, loved the wrong man, and may have known the one secret the mob could not afford to let reach the FBI.

In September 1984, Mary Bari was lured to a Brooklyn social club with what sounded like a simple opportunity: a waitressing job. But the men waiting for her were not offering work. They were protecting a secret. Bari had been involved with Alphonse “Allie Boy” Persico, the son of Colombo boss Carmine Persico, and when Allie Boy went on the run, the family feared Mary knew where he was hiding.

That fear was enough.

Inside the club, Gregory “The Grim Reaper” Scarpa and other Colombo figures turned suspicion into execution. Mary Bari disappeared into the darkest side of Mafia paranoia — the side where even girlfriends, witnesses, and women outside the life could be killed if they knew too much.

snippet.title: The Dark Reason Mafia Buried Israel Greenwald Under Concrete
snippet.description:
Israel Greenwald was not a mob boss. He was not a hitman. He was not a gangster fighting for territory in Brooklyn. He was a jeweler, a husband, and a father who walked into a criminal nightmare because dangerous men believed he knew too much.

In 1986, Greenwald became connected to a stolen bond scheme involving Burton Kaplan, a longtime underworld figure who later became the key witness in the Mafia Cops case. Kaplan feared Greenwald might cooperate with investigators and expose the scheme. In the Mafia world, fear was enough. Suspicion was enough. And when Kaplan wanted Greenwald gone, he did not just call ordinary killers.

He called men with badges.

Louis Eppolito and Stephen Caracappa were NYPD detectives. They had police authority, flashing lights, access to information, and the power to make an innocent man trust them. According to court records, the detectives pulled Greenwald over, told him he was needed in a hit-and-run investigation, and made him follow them. He thought he was dealing with police officers.

Instead, he was being delivered to his own murder.

Greenwald was taken to a Brooklyn garage, shot, buried in a hole, and covered with concrete. For nineteen years, his family had no body, no grave, and no real answer. Then, after the Mafia Cops case finally cracked open, investigators found his remains beneath the floor.

localized.title: The Dark Reason Mafia Buried Israel Greenwald Under Concrete
localized.description:
Israel Greenwald was not a mob boss. He was not a hitman. He was not a gangster fighting for territory in Brooklyn. He was a jeweler, a husband, and a father who walked into a criminal nightmare because dangerous men believed he knew too much.

In 1986, Greenwald became connected to a stolen bond scheme involving Burton Kaplan, a longtime underworld figure who later became the key witness in the Mafia Cops case. Kaplan feared Greenwald might cooperate with investigators and expose the scheme. In the Mafia world, fear was enough. Suspicion was enough. And when Kaplan wanted Greenwald gone, he did not just call ordinary killers.

He called men with badges.

Louis Eppolito and Stephen Caracappa were NYPD detectives. They had police authority, flashing lights, access to information, and the power to make an innocent man trust them. According to court records, the detectives pulled Greenwald over, told him he was needed in a hit-and-run investigation, and made him follow them. He thought he was dealing with police officers.

Instead, he was being delivered to his own murder.

Greenwald was taken to a Brooklyn garage, shot, buried in a hole, and covered with concrete. For nineteen years, his family had no body, no grave, and no real answer. Then, after the Mafia Cops case finally cracked open, investigators found his remains beneath the floor.

How Israel Greenwald became trapped in a stolen bond scheme he may not have fully understood
Why Burton Kaplan feared Greenwald might cooperate with police
How Kaplan became connected to Louis Eppolito and Stephen Caracappa
Why the Mafia Cops were more dangerous than ordinary hitmen
How police badges were used to pull Greenwald over and make him obey
What happened inside the Brooklyn garage where Greenwald vanished
Why his body was buried under concrete for nearly two decades
How his disappearance destroyed his family’s life and left them without closure
Why Greenwald’s murder became one of the darkest pieces of the Mafia Cops case
How Anthony “Gaspipe” Casso later used the same corrupt police pipeline for other murders
Why the Eppolito and Caracappa case exposed one of the worst betrayals in NYPD history
How the discovery of Greenwald’s remains helped prove the truth hidden for nineteen years

snippet.title: Ethel Kennedy – Das tragische Schicksal ihrer 11 Kinder
snippet.description:
Ethel Kennedy galt als das unzerbrechliche Rückgrat der berühmtesten Familie Amerikas. Nach der Ermordung ihres Mannes Robert F. Kennedy (Bobby) zog sie 11 Kinder alleine auf. Doch was kaum jemand erzählt, ist das, was danach geschah. Dieses Video erzählt die wahre Geschichte der Kennedy-Familie und zeigt, warum selbst Historiker vom "Kennedy-Fluch" sprechen.  Von den 11 Kindern führte keines ein gewöhnliches Leben. Wir blicken hinter die verschlossenen Türen von Hickory Hill und erzählen, wie der Mord an Bobby das Leben seiner Kinder für immer zerstörte.  In diesem Video erfährst du:Warum David Kennedy den Tod seines Vaters nie verkraftete und ein tragisches Ende fand.  Wie Michael Kennedy bei einem familiären Skiunfall in Aspen starb.  Welcher Skandal Robert Kennedy Jr. fast zerstörte, bevor er Präsident werden wollte.  Das stille Leid der Töchter Kathleen und Kerry.  Wie Ethel Kennedy trotz des Verlustes von Ehemann, Söhnen, Enkeln und Urenkeln bis zu ihrem 96. Lebensjahr nicht zerbrach.  Wenn dich amerikanische Dynastien, wahre Familiengeschichten, politische Tragödien und die dunklen Seiten berühmter Namen interessieren, dann abonniere den Kanal.Schreib in die Kommentare:

snippet.title: The Real War Dogs: Inside the Most Insane Arms Deal in The U.S. History
snippet.description:
Two Miami Beach kids. A strip mall office above a laundromat. A $298 million Pentagon contract to arm the Afghan National Army with 100 million rounds of ammunition. This is the true story of Efraim Diveroli and David Packouz, the founders of AEY Incorporated, who beat Lockheed Martin and General Dynamics at the Pentagon’s own bidding game, then nearly armed an entire foreign military with 40-year-old rotting Chinese ammunition smuggled through Albania.

In this deep-dive investigation, you’ll learn:
• How Efraim Diveroli, at just 21 years old, exploited the Federal Business Opportunities website like an eBay loophole
 • The exact mechanics of how AEY undercut major defense contractors by $53 million
 • Why Chinese-made ammunition was illegal under U.S. law and how AEY allegedly repackaged it in cardboard boxes to hide its origin
 • The role of Albanian businessman Kosta Trebicka and the secret phone recordings that brought everything down
 • How New York Times reporter C.J. Chivers exposed the entire operation in March 2008
 • The mysterious mountain road death of the only witness who could have named names
 • The 71 federal counts, prison sentences, and how the Pentagon’s entire small-business contracting system was overhauled

Key figures: 
Efraim Diveroli (CEO, AEY Inc.), David Packouz (Vice President), Kosta Trebicka (Albanian supplier), C.J. Chivers (NYT investigative reporter), Senator Carl Levin (Senate Armed Services Committee).

Timeline: 
2005 founding of AEY operations, January 2007 contract award, March 2008 NYT exposé, September 2008 death of Kosta Trebicka, 2009 federal sentencing.

This story matters because it exposed the dangerous gap in how the U.S. military vets the people who arm its allies. The reforms that followed AEY shaped every Pentagon small business contract written in the years since. It’s also the story behind the Hollywood film “War Dogs,” though the truth is far darker than the movie ever showed.

 • U.S. House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform Report on AEY (June 2008)
